lists.title: Tagalog A1 Grammar Path
lists.description: First Tagalog: the ang/ng/sa marker system, actor-focus verbs with -um-, the na linker, the mga plural marker, may/wala existence and possession, and hindi negation.

points.title: The ang phrase marks the sentence's topic
points.explanation: Tagalog doesn't have a fixed "subject" the way English does. Instead, one noun phrase — marked by ang — is the TOPIC: the participant the sentence is "about," chosen by which role the verb's affix highlights. Kumain ang bata ("The child ate") marks the eater (bata) as topic because kumain is an actor-focus verb.

drills.hint: ang — marks the actor as the topic, since kumain is actor-focus
ang — the drinker is the topic here
ang — marks the topic noun phrase

points.title: ng marks a non-topic actor, object, or possessor
points.function: Mark a noun that isn't the topic
points.explanation: ng (pronounced "nang") marks a noun phrase that ISN'T the topic — often the object when the actor is topic, or a possessor: Kumain ang bata ng pagkain ("The child ate [some] food") marks pagkain with ng because it's the object, not the topic. The same ng also shows possession: bahay ng kaibigan ("friend's house").

drills.hint: ng — marks the object, since it isn't the topic here
ng — also marks a possessor: "house OF friend"
ng — possessor marker

points.title: sa marks location, direction, or a specific place
points.explanation: sa introduces location or direction — "in," "at," "to": Pumunta ang bata sa bahay ("The child went to the house"). It's also used for definite/specific places and times.

drills.translation: The child went to the house.
drills.hint: sa — marks the destination

drills.translation: The man drank at the house.
drills.hint: sa — marks the location
sa — marks the location

points.title: Actor-focus verbs with the -um- infix
points.function: Build actor-focus verbs from a root
points.explanation: Many Tagalog action verbs form their actor-focus version by inserting -um- right after the root's first consonant: kain ("eat") → kumain; bili ("buy") → bumili. If the root starts with a vowel, -um- simply attaches to the front instead: inom ("drink") → uminom.

drills.hint: ate — kain + -um- infix after the first consonant
drank — inom + -um-, attaches to the front since the root starts with a vowel
bought — bili + -um- infix

points.title: The linker na
points.function: Connect a describing word to what it describes
points.explanation: na links a describing word to what it describes, in either order — noun + na + adjective: bata na mabuti ("a good child"). In fast speech na often shortens to -ng and attaches to the previous word if it ends in a vowel (batang mabuti), but na is the safe default to write.

drills.hint: na — links the noun to the adjective that follows
na — the linker between noun and adjective
na — linker

points.title: mga marks the plural
points.explanation: Tagalog nouns don't change form for plural — instead, the particle mga (pronounced "mah-NGA") goes right before the noun: bata ("child") → mga bata ("children"); bahay ("house") → mga bahay ("houses").

drills.hint: mga — plural marker, placed before the noun
mga — same marker makes any noun plural
mga — plural marker

points.title: Existence and possession: may and wala
points.function: Say that something exists, or that you have it
points.explanation: may states that something exists or that someone has something: May pagkain ako, literally "there-is food I," means "I have food." Its negative wala says the opposite: Wala pagkain ako would be "I have no food."

drills.hint: may — states existence/possession; "ako" (I) follows the noun
may — existence/possession marker
wala — the negative of may

points.title: hindi negates verbs and adjectives
points.function: Say what isn't true or didn't happen
points.explanation: hindi is the general negator for verbs and adjectives — placed right before what it negates: Hindi kumain ang bata ("The child didn't eat"), Hindi malaki ang bahay ("The house isn't big").

drills.hint: hindi — negates the verb, placed right before it
hindi — negates the adjective
hindi — general negator
